C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:

-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

By the definition of scalar multiplication in a semialgebra, this mapping can be rewritten using the algebra map of \( B \). Through a series of substitutions and applications of algebraic identities—specifically the definition of scalar multiplication and the fact that multiplying by one leaves the element unchanged—we establish the required equality.

This equality holds because ψ not only preserves the algebraic operations but also respects the scalar multiplication structure dictated by φ. Thus, the property is established for any semialgebraic homomorphism, scalar, and element within the structure.
